description: Check whether email addresses can receive mail, up to 50,000 addresses a call (an input size per request, not a volume cap: send more in further calls or as a background job); a call over it is refused with TOO_MANY_EMAILS, free. What our probe pacing cannot check now is queued into a verification job and comes back `queued` with its `job_id`, free here and billed when the job checks it. Each result has `status` (valid, invalid, catch-all or unknown), `reason`, `reason_text`, `score` (0 to 100), `recommendation` (send, send_with_caution, retry_later or do_not_send), `charged`, `flags`, `smtp_code`, `catch_all_tier`, `did_you_mean` (a likely domain typo), `mail_provider` and `checked_at`. Costs $0.003 per valid or invalid result, drawn from your balance; catch-all and unknown results are free (pricing_get lists which statuses are charged). When the balance covers only some addresses, the rest come back `unknown` with reason `not_checked_insufficient_credits`, free (`not_checked_key_cap` when the key's monthly cap stops it). `depth: "quick"` never contacts the mail server: syntax, disposable and free lists, DNS, parked and new-domain flags and a recently measured catch-all verdict, at $0.001 per address whatever the status; an address that needs a mailbox check comes back `unknown` with reason `not_probed`. `depth: "cache"` (or `cache_only: true`) answers only from verdicts already on record from any account (valid within 30 days, invalid within 90): it never contacts the mail server and never counts against the probe budget, a known verdict is billed like a full check, and anything not on record comes back `miss`, free. A `paced` or `provider_cooldown` result carries `retry_after_s`: retry after that many seconds.

cache_only.description: Same as depth cache: answer from verdicts already on record, never contact the mail server.

depth.description: full (default) checks the mailbox; quick is DNS and lists only, $0.001 per address; cache answers only from verdicts already on record (miss is free).

emails.description: The addresses to check, up to 50,000 a call (an input size per request, not a volume cap: send more in further calls or as a background job). An item may be {email, first_name, last_name} to also check the address against the person's name.
